analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (18 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities fell for a second day on Tuesday: Dow -1.64%, S&P 500 -1.03%, Nasdaq -0.74%, Russell 2000 -1.49%. Decliners outnumbered gainers nearly 6:1, the third-worst breadth reading year to date, and all sectors closed lower.
The S&P 500 closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since early April. The 10-day cumulative advance/decline is below -400, down from +921 on 21-Oct.
The AI trade did not bounce. Semiconductors, memory and neoclouds were mostly lower and Nvidia fell again on tighter export controls and concerns about funding the AI buildout.

Factor rotation was sharp. Low volatility (SPLV) beat high beta (SPHB) by over 460 bp and quality (QUAL) beat it by 280 bp over five days. BofA notes AI groups still rank top on its Triple Momentum screen, which it reads as intact earnings momentum. Mizuho calls the selloff an indiscriminate buyers strike driven by systematic degrossing.

October US retail sales rose 0.2% m/m, in line with consensus. Ex-autos (+0.6% vs +0.4% consensus) and control group (+0.6% vs +0.3%) beat, and September was revised higher. Industrial production unexpectedly fell, import and export prices were well above expectations, and NAHB homebuilder sentiment hit a 14-year low.

Fedspeak was hawkish. St. Louis Fed's Musalem (non-voter) argued for several hikes and a 2-2.5% real policy rate by spring. Williams said conditions do not warrant aggressive action. The October FOMC held at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents for a 25 bp hike, and a December hike is largely priced.

BofA and Goldman Sachs each added a third 25 bp hike to their forecasts (Goldman for Mar-27). Waller flagged the potential for a 50 bp December hike if inflation runs hot. The October FOMC minutes are due Wednesday 14:00 ET, and previews call them somewhat stale.

Nvidia reports Q3 on 17-Nov after the close. The Street expects a beat and raise, and the focus is on FY28 guidance of about 70% revenue growth, export restrictions and AI infrastructure funding. Huang said he would return as CEO if the board asked, and the board said a return is not under consideration.

The US Commerce Department issued an interim rule requiring a US license for exports of advanced AI chips to non-US data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. China called the move unjustified and said it would take necessary measures.

European equities closed sharply lower: DAX -2%, FTSE 100 -1.8%, CAC -1.6%. Tech, miners, luxury and autos led declines on AI return concerns and weak China data, while energy and travel and leisure held up best.

German November ZEW was 35.6 vs 28.1 prior and 29.0 expected, the highest since February. UK unemployment was 4.6%, but payrolled employees fell 34K in October and regular pay growth slowed to 3.5%. A December BoE hike is seen as unlikely to be deterred, though most economists expect a hold in December.
Spain's de Cos is the front-runner to succeed Lagarde as ECB president after Knot withdrew. A formal decision is expected at the 26-27 November EU summit.

In France, Le Pen's pension plan and Ukraine stance drove the campaign. The OAT-Bund spread narrowed 3 bp to 152 bp. Goldman still sees Le Pen as the clear favourite and expects French bonds to underperform EU peers through mid-2027.

Asian equities fell: Nikkei -1.34%, Hang Seng -1.03%, Shanghai Composite -0.50%. South Korea and Taiwan saw steep declines. China pure-play AI model developers reliant on Nvidia hardware fell, while SMIC, Hua Hong and Cambricon outperformed.

RBA minutes showed the board debated holding versus hiking in November. Bullock said inflation risks are skewed to the upside. NZ inflation expectations support a December RBNZ hike, and Japan's Q3 GDP miss does not change December BOJ hike calls.
Economists called China's October activity data bearish: retail growth softened, fixed asset investment lagged, and 2027 growth is forecast to slow to 4.0-4.5%.
Trump meets Xi at APEC in Shenzhen this week. Little concrete progress is expected, the US-China trade truce runs through 10-Jan, and the G20 summit follows on Dec 14-15.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman Sachs upgraded to buy from neutral, citing EBITDA growth potential from natural and organic exposure, improved execution and network optimization. Shares rose 7.4%.
Bernstein downgraded to underperform from market perform, expecting an EPS miss next year on North America pressure. Shares fell 3%.
Morgan Stanley cut Moncler to underweight on heavy Asia exposure (~66% of sales), declining like-for-like volumes and margin pressure, and cut 2027/28 EPS well below consensus.
Oddo downgraded Stellantis to underperform, expecting raw-material and electronic-component inflation to limit savings, leaving 2027 AOI margin at 1.6% and industrial free cash flow at -€2.2B.
Oddo downgraded JCDecaux to neutral. The re-rating to 16x 2027 earnings leaves limited upside despite 6.1% organic growth expected in 2026 and 4.3% in 2027.
Barclays downgraded Swiss Life to equal weight. Shares trade at a premium to the sector, and lower Swiss rates and higher minimum guarantees pressure margins.
Barclays reinstated Zurich Insurance at equal weight. It sees limited near-term upside as global commercial P&C softens, with EPS growth only marginally ahead of consensus.
Goldman Sachs initiated SBM Offshore at buy as the FPSO leader (~40% share) best placed for the deepwater cycle in Guyana, Brazil and West Africa. 2027 award announcements are the key catalyst.
Goodbody initiated Barclays at buy, seeing the greatest re-rating potential from stronger execution, diversified revenue and better capital allocation.

sector_views.rationale: Energy outperformed in both US and European sessions during the selloff.
Software lagged in US trading, alongside homebuilders, managed care, banks and payments.
European luxury fell on softer China demand, with Moncler cut to underweight at Morgan Stanley.

earnings_insights: Home Depot Q3 reported: comps +2.2%, 50 bp better than consensus. Gross margin missed by 20 bp, EPS was slightly ahead, and the implied Q4 guide was seen as light. CFO Richard McPhail becomes CEO on 23-Nov. Shares -2.5%.

Walt Disney FQ4 reported: EPS, revenue and free cash flow all beat. Entertainment revenue was the upside driver on stronger subscription fees. Q1 operating income guided ahead and FY27 EPS growth guidance reaffirmed. Shares -1.5%.
Nike investor day: guided FY31 operating margin and EPS better than expected but guided FY28 lower. Shares -6.3%.
Energizer FQ4 reported: earnings and margins beat, revenue largely in line, and organic growth decline narrower than consensus. Shares +12.6%.
AECOM FQ4 reported: EPS and EBITDA modestly beat, net service revenue in line, backlog +13% y/y to $28B, and FY27 guidance largely in line with organic revenue growth of 4-6%. Shares +11.1%.
Amer Sports Q3 reported: beat, FY guidance raised for all three segments, and a $1B buyback announced. Shares +3.9%.
Omeros Q3 reported: earnings better but revenue missed, and R&D expenses were above consensus. Shares -16.6%.
Nvidia Q3 results were due 17-Nov after the close. The Street expects a beat and raise, and the report is a preview, not a result. FY28 guidance is for about 70% revenue growth.
Walmart, Target, TJX, Lowe's and Ross Stores report this week.
NIBE Q3 reported: revenue SEK 11.23B vs SEK 11.08B estimate, operating income SEK 1.52B vs SEK 1.42B consensus, EPS SEK 0.44 vs SEK 0.45 estimate. Shares -3.8%.
Diploma FY26 reported: EPS growth 45%, organic revenue growth 15%. FY27 guidance is 12% revenue growth and a 25.5% EBITA margin. Shares -2.4%.
Dassault Systemes Capital Markets Day: targets 2029 revenue above €8B and non-IFRS diluted EPS of €1.80. Shares -4.9%.

Beat consensus, and September was revised higher.

risk_factors: Tighter US export controls on AI chips and concerns about funding the AI infrastructure buildout.
Hawkish Fed path: a December hike is priced, and Waller flagged a possible 50 bp move if inflation runs hot.
Hot import and export prices, and an unexpected decline in industrial production.
The S&P 500 break below its 200-day average and weak breadth could extend systematic degrossing.
French political and fiscal risk ahead of the election, with Goldman expecting French bonds to underperform through mid-2027.
China growth slowdown and the overhang from US tech restrictions.
vol_and_positioning: Breadth was the third-worst reading year to date, with S&P decliners outnumbering gainers by nearly 6:1.
Low volatility (SPLV) and quality (QUAL) outperformed high beta (SPHB) by over 460 bp and 280 bp over five days.
Mizuho attributes the selloff to systematic degrossing, which it calls an indiscriminate buyers strike.
BofA says AI groups remain top-ranked on its Triple Momentum screen even though photonics, data centers and AI compute are among the worst one-month performers.
geopolitical: The US Commerce Department's interim rule requires licenses for advanced AI chip exports to non-US data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. China called it unjustified and said it would take necessary measures.
Trump attends the ASEAN meeting in the Philippines, then the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, with bilateral talks with Xi and a trilateral with Xi and Putin. Little concrete progress is expected.
The US has complained about the pace of Chinese rare-earth shipments and lower Chinese purchases of US agriculture. The G20 leaders' summit is in Florida on Dec 14-15.
Le Pen said she would end new French financial aid to Ukraine if elected while honouring existing commitments.
Nvidia set up a board-level committee on national security and export controls. Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee on 1-Dec.
cross_bank_references: Goldman highlighting upward revisions and accelerating real core sales growth, though Citi flagged uneven demand.
BofA expects the minutes to reveal a deeper committee divide than the two formal dissents suggested, and its team recently added a third 25 bp hike to its forecast.
Goldman Sachs has also added a third 25 bp hike (in Mar-27) to its rate path.
Goldman Sachs still sees Le Pen as the clear favourite, Morgan Stanley expects the 2027 budget to pass close to the draft, and Barclays sees early-2027 polls as a key catalyst.
